// Every subtest here has the required t.Run signature and the required
// testing.TB receiver, and every one of them asserts against the parent test.
// The callback shape alone cannot tell these from the target shape.
package fixture

import (
	"testing"

	qt "github.com/frankban/quicktest"
)

func assertThrough(c *qt.C) {
	c.Check(1, qt.Equals, 1)
}

func TestBorrowedChecker(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)

	t.Run("asserts through the parent checker", func(t *testing.T) {
		c.Assert(2, qt.Equals, 2)
	})

	t.Run("hands the parent checker to a helper", func(t *testing.T) {
		assertThrough(c)
	})

	t.Run("builds a checker from the parent TB", func(subT *testing.T) {
		subT.Log("the parameter is not the TB this checker is built from")
		inner := qt.New(t)
		inner.Assert(3, qt.Equals, 3)
	})
}

func TestNestedBorrowedChecker(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)

	t.Run("outer", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Run("inner", func(t *testing.T) {
			c.Assert(4, qt.Equals, 4)
		})
	})
}

func BenchmarkBorrowedChecker(b *testing.B) {
	c := qt.New(b)

	b.Run("subbenchmark", func(b *testing.B) {
		c.Assert(5, qt.Equals, 5)
	})
}

func FuzzBorrowedChecker(f *testing.F) {
	c := qt.New(f)

	f.Fuzz(func(t *testing.T, input string) {
		c.Assert(input, qt.Not(qt.Equals), "")
	})
}
